summary: Three issues remain: the empty tmpfs invocation lacks the Codex non-repository override, the implementation fingerprint is not defined over a closed file set, and rotating refresh tokens still have crash and external-writer races.

recommendations.location: Architecture: the container as the boundary — Codex invocation; Container lifecycle, step 2
recommendations.issue: [P1] The working directory is defined as a fresh, unconditionally empty tmpfs, but the complete Codex argv never includes `--skip-git-repo-check`. Codex versions requiring a Git repository will exit before reaching the API, so the schema gate and control-reachability checks cannot succeed.
recommendations.suggestion: Add `--skip-git-repo-check` to the pinned argv, invocation profile, policy validator, and tests, or create a controlled repository in the tmpfs before execution and fingerprint that setup.

recommendations.location: Premises / live-evidence — host_impl_digest; Installer & skill dispatch, steps 2–6
recommendations.issue: [P1] The fingerprint is described as a tree/package digest but its enumerated coverage omits `install.py`/`install.sh` and covers only the SKILL.md “dispatch lines.” Other SKILL.md instructions and installer logic control gating, activation, retries, and publication; changing them can therefore leave live evidence apparently current. The treatment of generated evidence files is also not explicit, making “rehash the installed tree and compare it to host_impl_digest” ambiguous or self-referential.
recommendations.suggestion: Define a mechanically closed digest file set covering every immutable installed file, including both complete SKILL.md files, installers, helpers, fixtures, and policy data. Keep generated manifest/evidence artifacts outside that digest or define explicit exclusions and bind them through a separate release digest, then verify both before activation.

recommendations.location: The credential — broker lifecycle and concurrency; Risks and mitigations
recommendations.issue: [P2] Local locking and atomic persistence do not make refresh-token rotation transactional with the provider. If the provider invalidates token R0 and returns R1, a crash before R1 is durably replaced leaves only invalid R0. A normal host Codex process also does not honor the broker’s private lock and can race the broker’s refresh. The concurrent-broker test does not cover either case, so the claim that rotation cannot invalidate host authentication is unsupported.
recommendations.suggestion: Establish the real provider’s rotation, grace-period, and recovery semantics. Prefer token exchange that leaves the durable host credential unchanged; otherwise coordinate every credential writer, add concurrent host-CLI and crash-injection tests around the refresh-response/persistence boundary, and fail closed or narrow the host-auth preservation claim when recoverability cannot be guaranteed.
